lesson.label: 📖 Bài học chính
lesson.title: 1. Happy: I’m on cloud nine!
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Linh has just had a phone call from HR. She rushes over to tell her colleague Mark the news.*
lines: Hey, Linh. You're **grinning**. Anything good happen?
Yes! HR just called me. I got the promotion!
Really? That’s **wonderful news**! Congratulations! You must be really **excited!**
I am. **To be honest, I still can’t quite believe it.** After the interview, I **was sure I didn’t get it**, because I was so nervous and I **forgot** some of my answers.
Well, they clearly **didn’t mind**. You’ve worked really hard this year, so you **completely deserve it**.
Thank you. Right now, I mostly just feel **relieved**. I’ve been **worrying about it** all week.
**I could tell.** You kept checking your phone during the meeting this morning.
Haha, **you noticed**? When they told me, I **couldn’t stop smiling**. I called my mum **straight away**, and she was **over the moon**.
That’s lovely. I’m sure she’s **really proud of** you. All your hard work has finally **paid off**. So, what changes now?
From next month, I’ll **be in charge of** the design team. It’s **a big step** for me, so I feel **a little nervous about it**.
**I wouldn't worry too much.** Everyone already **trusts** you and **asks you for advice**, so I’m sure you’ll **do a great job**.
Thanks, Mark. **That really means a lot.** Would you like to get dinner after work to **celebrate**? **It’s my treat.**
**I’d love to.** And well done, Linh. **You’ve earned it.**

lesson.title: About a time you felt really happy
head: Purposes
Phrases
rows: **When? What was happening?**

• **This happened a few years ago, when I was…**
• **At that time, I was really looking forward to…**
• **I had been waiting for this moment for a long time.**
• **I was a little nervous because…**
**What happened?**

• **Then, something unexpected happened.**
• **Suddenly, I got a call / received some good news.**
• **I couldn't believe it when…**
• **As soon as I heard the news, I…**
**How did you feel? How did you show it?**

• **I was so happy / excited / surprised.**
• **I couldn't stop smiling.**
• **I was grinning from ear to ear.**
• **I felt so relieved because…**
• **I was so happy that I wanted to tell everyone.**
**Why was it so special?**

• **It meant a lot to me because…**
• **I had worked really hard for it.**
• **It was the first time I had ever…**
• **It was a special moment for me because…**
**How did you celebrate? How do you feel now?**

• **I celebrated by…**
• **I called my family / friends to share the news.**
• **We went out for dinner to celebrate.**
• **It's still one of my happiest memories.**

lesson.title: 2. Frustrated: It’s driving me up the wall!
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Tom notices his colleague Hà glaring at her laptop.*
lines: Hà, are you OK? You look **a bit upset**.
Not really. You know the presentation **I’ve been working on** for two weeks?
The one for the new client? Yes, of course.
They’ve just emailed me. They want to **change the whole idea**, and the meeting is on Friday!
I know. I’m **so annoyed**. **The worst part is**, they **agreed to** everything last week. Now two weeks of work are **a complete waste of time**.
**I’d be annoyed too.** Have you called them?
Yes, three times, but nobody answered. And it’s the second time this month. I’m **really tired of** clients **changing their minds at the last minute**.
**I understand.** But **try not to take it personally**. They do the same thing with everyone.
I know you’re right, but I’m just **too angry to think clearly** right now.
**Look on the bright side.** Your research and data are still useful, so you **don’t have to start from scratch.**
Hmm, **that’s true**. **At least** I don’t have to do everything again.
Why don’t we **take a short break** and get a coffee? You can **get it all off your chest**, and then we can **make a new plan** together.
Thanks, Tom. That **sounds good**. I need to **calm down** first, or I might send them an angry email that **I’ll regret** later.

lesson.title: About a time you felt really frustrated
head: Purposes
Phrases
rows: **What were you trying to do?**

• **A few weeks ago, I was trying to…**
• **I wanted to…, but…**
• **Everything was going well until…**
**What went wrong?**

• **Suddenly, …**
• **Just when I thought everything was OK, …**
• **To make things worse, …**
**How did you feel?**

• **I was really annoyed / frustrated.**
• **I was getting more and more frustrated.**
• **It really got on my nerves.**
• **It was really annoying because…**
**How did you deal with it?**

• **I took a deep breath and tried again.**
• **I decided to take a short break.**
• **I talked to a friend about it.**
• **I asked someone for help.**
• **After a while, I managed to…**
**What do you think about it now?**

• **Looking back, I think I was too stressed about it.**
• **Now I know I should…**
• **It taught me to be more patient. At least, I learned something from the experience.**

homework.title: Part 1: Vocab check
homework.instructions: Fill in each blank with a word or phrase from the word bank. Use each one once.
homework.context: Lisa tells her friend Tom about her mum's birthday last weekend.
lines: It was great in the end, but the morning was really {frustrating}.
I ordered a chocolate cake from a bakery two weeks ago. Then, on Saturday morning, they called and said they couldn't make it because their oven was broken. They told me at {the last minute}!
I was. And {the worst part is}, I'd already paid for it!
First, I took a deep breath to {calm down}. Then my sister told me to {look on the bright side}. At least we still had time to bake a cake ourselves.
Yes! It took three hours, and it looked a bit strange, but Mum was {over the moon}. She said it was her best present ever.
Aw, she must be really {proud of} you two.
I think so. I felt so {relieved}, because I was {worried about} it all morning.
Sounds like the broken oven was a good thing after all!

homework.title: Part 2: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to Hoa talking about her first day at a new company, then answer the questions.

script.text: Hi, I'm Hoa. Last Monday was my first day at a new company, and I was really nervous. ==I wanted to make a good first impression==, so I left home early.
But on the way, ==the bus broke down==, and I had to wait twenty minutes for another one. In the end, I arrived ten minutes late. I was so annoyed with myself.

To make things worse, my computer wasn't ready, so I couldn't do any real work all morning. ==I just sat there and read some documents.== It was really frustrating, because I wanted to show everyone that I was a hard worker.

Then, at lunchtime, something nice happened. My manager took the whole team out for lunch ==to welcome me==. Everyone was so friendly, and they told me funny stories about their first days. One colleague said ==he got lost in the building== on his first day!
I felt so relieved. By the afternoon, my computer was working, and I finished my first small task.
Looking back, I think I worried too much. Now I always tell myself: one bad morning doesn't mean a bad day.

questions.q: Why did Hoa leave home early?
options: She wanted to buy breakfast on the way.
She wanted her new team to have a good opinion of her.
Her manager asked her to come in early.
questions.why: “I wanted to make a good first impression, so I left home early.”

options: There was a problem with her bus.
She got lost in the building.
questions.why: “On the way, the bus broke down.”

questions.q: What did Hoa do in the morning?
options: She had a meeting with her manager.
questions.why: “I just sat there and read some documents.”

questions.q: Why did the manager take the team out for lunch?
options: To welcome a new member of the team
questions.why: “My manager took the whole team out for lunch to welcome me.”

questions.q: What did one colleague say about his first day?
options: He couldn't find his way around the building.
questions.why: “He got lost in the building on his first day!”
